main_body: Flat snow ground tile pattern: pale blue-white snow with dark grey-green mottled clumps repeating across the patch. No standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain ground tile, no standing object; the scan shows alternating light snow and dark clump runs, not a top/front structure)
evidence: The kind is terrain: a seamless ground surface patch, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top and front contract does not apply. It has no standing volume, no isometric side face and no flat elevation drawn as an object. The column scan shows only alternating snow and dark patches of the ground texture.

style.evidence: The candidate has 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against the grass reference's 80 colours and 26 per tile. It is comparable to the paving reference (7 colours, 7 per tile), but well under the grass. It has 0% flat-fill coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so its dark tones are tinted grey-green rather than near-black. It carries speckled dither texture in the dark clumps and light snow. The palette is limited to about 5 usable steps (white highlight, pale, light blue, grey-green, dark green-grey), shallower than the grass but not a flat sticker. The pattern repeats with strong regularity, and the dark clumps read as a tiled motif instead of natural snow. A careful artist would find it thinner than the grass reference, so it fails.
